questions.q: Given a chunk of token ids of length T+1, how are the training inputs and targets built?
options: inputs = chunk[:, 1:], targets = chunk[:, :-1]
inputs = chunk[:, :-1], targets = chunk[:, 1:] — the same sequence shifted by one position
Two completely separate sequences must be loaded for inputs and targets
inputs and targets are identical copies of chunk
questions.explain: Next-token prediction uses one sequence for both: inputs drop the last token, targets drop the first, so targets[t] is always the token that actually follows inputs[t].

questions.q: Why does the training step call logits.reshape(-1, vocab_size) and targets.reshape(-1) before computing the loss?
options: To reduce memory usage by discarding most of the logits
Because F.cross_entropy expects a 2D input of shape (N, C) and a 1D target of shape (N,), so batch and sequence dimensions must be flattened together
Because PyTorch cannot process 3D tensors
To convert the logits into probabilities before the loss
questions.explain: cross_entropy's standard signature compares (N, C) class scores against (N,) target class indices, so the batch and time dimensions of a (B, T, vocab_size) tensor are flattened into one N dimension.

questions.q: What does torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ do, and when is it called?
options: It zeroes out all gradients; called before the forward pass
It rescales the gradient vector so its total norm doesn't exceed max_norm; called after backward() and before optimizer.step()
It clips the loss value itself to a maximum before backward()
It removes dropout layers during training
questions.explain: Gradient clipping caps the overall size of the gradient update (without changing its direction) after backward() computes gradients and before step() applies them, preventing a rare large gradient from destabilizing training.

questions.q: Why is AdamW typically preferred over plain SGD for training a transformer like TinyGPT?
options: AdamW is required by PyTorch for any model with attention layers
AdamW combines Adam's per-parameter adaptive learning rates with weight decay decoupled from the gradient update, which regularizes weights without distorting Adam's adaptive behavior
AdamW trains strictly faster in wall-clock time on any hardware
AdamW eliminates the need for gradient clipping
questions.explain: AdamW is Adam with weight decay applied directly to the weights rather than folded into the gradient, which is why it has become the standard default optimizer for transformer training.

questions.q: Why should model.train() be called before a training step if the model uses dropout?
options: It has no real effect; it's just a convention
It disables gradient tracking to speed up training
It activates dropout (and similar mode-dependent layers) so the model trains with its intended regularization, as opposed to eval mode where dropout is disabled
It resets the model's weights to their initial values
questions.explain: model.train() and model.eval() toggle layers like dropout and batch norm between their training and inference behavior; dropout should be active during training and disabled during evaluation or generation.
